facts.text: Redvale sits atop Wrights Mesa, bordered by Naturita Canyon to the southwest and Maverick Draw to the northeast.
The town was originally called Redlands, but the name changed to Redvale in 1909 after the post office rejected the earlier name.
Redvale was a frequent stopping place for travelers and freight wagons hauling copper and uranium ore from Paradox Valley to the railhead in Placerville.
The community lies within the watershed of the San Miguel River, which flows northwest to the Dolores River and eventually joins the Colorado River in Utah.
Redvale’s elevation is 6,483 feet, placing it high in the San Juan Mountains and offering access to the Uncompahgre National Forest.
The Redlands Townsite Company incorporated on August 31, 1907, and early years featured a hotel, general store, church, and post office that served the growing settlement.
